summary: Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1899–1904). He served at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and became Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Working in Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Voigt studied in Berlin under Lüders, Breloer, and Schaeder, and at Marburg (Ph.D.) under Nobel and Heiler. He was Director of the Oriental Division at the Royal Library of Berlin (1949–1976).

Wolfram Eberhard worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Berlin and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen under Ferdinand Lessing. He later served as Professor of Sinology at Ankara University (1937–1948) and Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).

Woncheol Yun is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woodford Wright Sherlock worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed an M.A. at Trinity College Dublin (1852) and served as Lecturer in Hindustani at University College London (1884) and the University of Cambridge (1883–1912).

Woosung Huh is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).
Wouter J. Hanegraaff works in religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (~1982–1995) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam (~1999).
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).

Władysław Kotwicz specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1891–1895) and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1923) and the University of Lviv (~1923–1944).
Włodzimir Szajan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Lviv (~1927–1939) under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak (~1930–1939).
Xi Cao works in computational studies and Tibetology, holding posts at Tibet University and Minzu University of China.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (completed by 2016) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Xianlin Ji worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tsinghua University and the University of Göttingen (PhD) under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He was long-affiliated with Peking University (professor from 1946; vice president 1978).

Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and Indology. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Peking University (~1946–1949), Academia Sinica (~1949–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Ghent University as a doctoral student and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).

Xiaoting Wei works in sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under Cheng Mei Ku (attested 2004) and served as Associate Lecturer at the Australian National University in 2016.

Xin Huang is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Sichuan Normal University and Sichuan University, and held professorships at Sichuan Minzu College (2012–2016), Sichuan Normal University (2016–2019), and Nanning Normal University (2023).

Xinchuan Huang worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Peking University (~1952–1958) and served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1998, attested 2007).

Xinguang Ma works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwest University and held a post at Shanxi Normal University's School of Chinese Language and Literature.

Xinru Liu works in Indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, later holding posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and The College of New Jersey.
